description: Tuning governing-rules set (#1867; held out until the applicability judge prompt was tuned on it in #1997 and #2005, so the tuning set since #2024): a synthetic retailer's information handling policy (40 atomic obligations) and analyst-worded requirements labelled with the rules that truly apply to each, a per-rule verdict, and the business fact a BA would supply when the verdict is needs-ba-input.

policy.title: Harbor Lane Outfitters — Information Handling Policy

annotation.labelledBy: claude-opus-5-5 (AI coding agent dispatched on #1867), not a person
annotation.procedure: The policy was written for this fixture in original wording, then each requirement was written in business language and labelled against policy-v1 before any arm ran. See ANNOTATION.md.

rules.summary: One named individual per sign-in identity; no sharing between people.
Administrative staff identities need a second sign-in factor.
Least privilege; broader permissions need the system owner's written approval.
A leaver's access is removed by the end of their final working day.
System owners review who holds access every quarter.
Customer sign-in locks for fifteen minutes after five failed attempts.
Internal application sessions end after thirty minutes of inactivity.
Permission changes are written to the audit trail with actor, subject and timestamp.
Bulk extraction of customer or financial records is audit-logged with actor, timestamp and scope.
Audit trail entries are tamper-proof, administrators included.
Security staff examine audit alerts at least monthly.
Audit trail entries are retained for at least one year.
Staff changes to prices, discounts or payment amounts are audit-logged with old and new values.
Financial transaction records are retained for seven years after fiscal year end.
Personal information of a closed customer account is erased or anonymised within ninety days.
Personal information copied into test or training environments is erased within thirty days.
Recorded support calls and chat transcripts are retained at most twelve months.
Each personal-information dataset has a named owner and a documented retention period.
Records under legal hold are never destroyed until the hold is lifted.
Personal and payment information is encrypted in transit.
Personal and payment information is encrypted at rest, backups included.
Full card numbers are never stored; only the last four digits.
Encryption keys rotate yearly and are held apart from the protected information.
Files of personal information sent to an outside party are protected for the intended recipient only.
Production changes are approved by someone other than their author before going live.
Changes are tested outside production before release.
Every production change has a documented undo path.
Emergency changes are reviewed and approved within two working days afterwards.
Customers get five working days' notice of planned downtime.
No standing developer write access to production data.
An outside company completes a security review and data protection agreement before it receives personal or payment information.
Outside companies handling personal information are re-assessed yearly.
Outside companies get only the information their service needs.
Outside company contracts require security incident notice within seventy-two hours.
A current register lists each outside company handling personal information and what it receives.
Personal information is collected only for a purpose stated at collection.
Marketing goes only to opted-in customers, with a one-step opt-out.
Requests to see held personal information are answered within thirty days.
Precise location needs explicit, withdrawable permission.
Personal information of children under sixteen needs verified parental consent.

items.title: Download last month's invoices
items.text: The accounts team want a button on the billing screen that downloads all of last month's invoices as one spreadsheet, so they can reconcile them against the bank statement.

applies.businessFact: Will each download be attributed to the person who ran it, with the date and the invoice period it covered?

items.title: Promote a colleague to team lead
items.text: A store manager can give any team member the team-lead role from the staff screen, which unlocks refunds and rota editing for that member.

applies.businessFact: Will each promotion be noted with who granted it, who received it and when?
Is the store manager the person the policy names as owner of the till and rota systems, and is their approval given in writing?

items.title: Nearest shops in the mobile app
items.text: The mobile app's store finder should show the three nearest shops based on where the phone is right now.

applies.businessFact: Will the app ask the shopper before reading the phone's position, and can they turn that off later?

items.title: Quick fixes to misspelt street names
items.text: Support should be able to ask engineering to correct misspelt street names straight in the order tables, to save time on parcels returned as undeliverable.

items.title: Seasonal holiday workers
items.text: Temporary holiday workers get logins for the rota and till systems for December; their last shift is usually on the second of January.

applies.businessFact: Who switches off a seasonal worker's logins, and does that happen on their last shift?

items.title: Satisfaction survey through SurveyCo
items.text: Send the list of last quarter's buyers to SurveyCo so they can email each buyer a short satisfaction questionnaire.

applies.businessFact: Has SurveyCo passed the supplier security review and signed the data protection agreement?
Which buyer details does SurveyCo need beyond an email address?
Will SurveyCo be added to the supplier register with the buyer details it gets?

items.title: Abandoned basket reminders
items.text: Email shoppers who left items in their basket a reminder twenty-four hours later, with a ten percent off code.

applies.businessFact: Will reminders go only to shoppers who agreed to promotional email, and can they stop them in a single click?

items.title: Junior rewards club
items.text: Launch a junior rewards club where youngsters aged twelve and below sign up with their name and birthday to get a treat on their special day.

applies.businessFact: Will a mum, dad or carer confirm each junior sign-up before it is accepted?

items.title: Hand parcels to FastShip
items.text: Pass each parcel's recipient name, phone number and address to the new courier, FastShip, through their booking system.

applies.businessFact: Has FastShip passed the supplier security review and signed the data protection agreement?
Will FastShip be added to the supplier register with the parcel details it gets?
Is the connection to FastShip's booking system secured end to end?

items.title: Stay signed in to the returns tool
items.text: Staff using the returns tool stay signed in for the whole shift, so they do not have to keep typing their password.

items.title: Yearly clear-out of old order emails
items.text: Purge every order confirmation email older than two years each January.

applies.businessFact: Will the January purge ever delete an email that is part of a dispute or lawsuit the legal team has asked us to preserve?

items.title: One login for the warehouse scanners
items.text: Pickers on the warehouse floor should all use one common username and password on the handheld scanners, so shifts can swap devices quickly.

items.title: Closing a customer account
items.text: When a customer closes their account, remove their name, email address and delivery addresses from our systems within one month, but keep their past orders for tax reporting.

applies.businessFact: How long will the past orders be kept after the account is closed?

items.title: Price match at the till
items.text: Store supervisors can override the price of any item at the checkout to match a competitor's advertised price.

applies.businessFact: Will the till keep the original price, the overridden price and the supervisor's name for each override?

items.title: Keep call recordings for coaching
items.text: Keep recordings of customer service phone calls for two years so team leaders can use them to coach new starters.

items.title: Realistic data on the staging site
items.text: Every night, copy the live order database to the staging site so testers can try new features on realistic data.

applies.businessFact: Is each nightly copy wiped within thirty days, or does staging keep old copies?

items.title: Authenticator app for back-office admins
items.text: Administrators of the online shop's back office must confirm each sign-in with a code from an authenticator app as well as their password.

items.title: Lock out repeated wrong passwords
items.text: After five wrong passwords in a row, a shopper's account should be locked for fifteen minutes before they can try again.

items.title: Remember full card details
items.text: Save shoppers' full card numbers so they can check out with one click next time.

items.title: Friday evening fixes
items.text: Let the lead developer push fixes to the live site on their own on Friday evenings, when nobody else is around to look at them.

applies.businessFact: Are the Friday fixes tried anywhere other than the live site before they go out?

items.title: Emergency checkout fixes
items.text: When checkout is down, the on-call engineer may deploy a fix immediately and must get sign-off from the head of engineering by the next working day.

applies.businessFact: Is there a written way to roll back an emergency fix if it makes things worse?

items.title: Announce planned maintenance
items.text: Announce planned maintenance of the online shop with a banner one week ahead and an email to every account holder.

items.title: Twice-yearly stock system access check
items.text: Twice a year, each department head should confirm who still needs access to the stock system and ask IT to remove the rest.

items.title: Customers ask for their data
items.text: Customers can ask for a copy of everything we hold about them, and we will email it to them within six weeks.

items.title: Newsletter box at checkout
items.text: On the checkout page, add a pre-ticked box that signs shoppers up to the weekly newsletter.

items.title: Payment provider review cycle
items.text: Our payment provider has been with us for five years; procurement only looks at them again when the contract renews every three years.

items.title: Breach notice in supplier contracts
items.text: New supplier contracts should require the supplier to tell us about any breach affecting our data within three days.

items.title: Customer database keys
items.text: The encryption keys for the customer database are changed every two years and stored on the same server as the database for speed.

items.title: Tidy up mistaken log entries
items.text: Give the IT manager a way to delete embarrassing audit trail entries that were made by mistake.

items.title: Year-end payroll file for the accountants
items.text: Send the year-end payroll file to our external accountants as a password-protected archive that only they can open.

applies.businessFact: Have the accountants passed the supplier security review and signed the data protection agreement?

items.title: Greener basket button
items.text: Change the colour of the add-to-basket button to dark green to match the new brand guide.

items.title: Most helpful reviews first
items.text: Show product reviews sorted by most helpful first, with newest first as a second option.

items.title: Shoe size guide
items.text: Add a size guide table to every shoe product page, showing UK, EU and US sizes side by side.

items.title: Estimated delivery dates
items.text: Display an estimated delivery date on each product page, worked out from the warehouse's current stock level for that product.

items.title: Filter the catalogue by material
items.text: Let shoppers filter the catalogue by colour and by material, such as leather, canvas or wool.

items.title: Rename the Specials menu
items.text: Rename the Specials menu to Offers across the website and the mobile app.
